question: Which fireplace system will be built: framed chase with manufactured firebox and Class A pipe, or site-built masonry?
why_it_matters: The system sets the footing cast in the slab, the chase framing method, and the roof penetration.
unblocks: Foundation/footing task, fireplace structure tasks and crew type, fireplace procurement lead item, chimney penetration framing

choices: Framed wood chase with manufactured wood-burning firebox and Class A pipe (as drawn p.5)
Site-built masonry fireplace and chimney
Modular masonry kit (e.g., Isokern) with lined chimney
Not selected yet — slab pour must wait for selection

question: How does the shed roof tie into the house: ledger on the brick wall below the eave, or into the existing roof plane?
why_it_matters: Tying into the roof plane adds existing-eave demolition and roof-to-roof work that a wall ledger does not.
unblocks: Tie-in demolition/prep tasks, ledger-through-veneer vs roof-cut tasks, flashing scope, framing duration

choices: Ledger through the brick veneer to wall framing below the existing eave
Cut back the existing eave/fascia and tie rafters into the existing roof framing
Beam on posts set against the house, no structural ledger
Unknown until the existing eave is opened

question: How do the roof support posts bear: turned-down footings in the new slab, separate piers, or existing deck framing?
why_it_matters: Post bearing must be built into the slab pour and the proposal's 'existing deck framing' does not exist on site.
unblocks: Footing/formwork tasks before the pour, post-base hardware procurement, framing sequence

choices: Turned-down thickened footings cast in the new patio slab at each post
Separate poured piers at the slab edge
Post bases anchored to the 4-inch slab only, no footing
There is an existing deck the posts tie into

question: Is the porch confirmed zero-electrical, or is the customer adding a fan, lights, or GFCI receptacle?
why_it_matters: Any add introduces a rough-electrical trade and inspection before the ceiling and screens close.
unblocks: Inclusion or omission of rough electrical, electrical inspection, fixture procurement

choices: Zero electrical confirmed — no rough-in
Add ceiling fan and/or lights
Add GFCI receptacle(s) only
Add fan, lights, and GFCI

question: Where does the fireplace sit: on the open outer wall per the plan, or on a side wall with the chimney through the shed roof?
why_it_matters: Location decides whether the chimney penetrates the new roof and how tall the chase must be against the main roof.
unblocks: Chimney penetration framing and flashing tasks, chase height, knee-wall/screen layout

choices: Centered on the open long side, chimney rising outside the roof edge (plan p.4)
On a side wall between screen bays, chimney through the new shed roof
Against the house near the ridge tie-in, chimney beside the main roof

question: Who sizes the rafters, ledger/beam, and posts — in-house per IRC tables or a structural engineer?
why_it_matters: An engineer adds a lead-time task before the framing package can be ordered.
unblocks: Engineering task and lead time, framing package procurement timing

choices: In-house per IRC prescriptive tables, no engineer
Structural engineer letter/stamp before framing
Engineer only if the AHJ requires it at permit review

question: Will a Johnson City building permit be pulled for the roof tie-in and wood-burning fireplace, and by whom?
why_it_matters: Proposal includes permitting but the breakdown carries none; permit and inspections gate framing and fireplace closure.
unblocks: Permit application task, framing and chimney inspection holds, pre-pour footing inspection

choices: Yes — contractor pulls a building permit with framing and fireplace/chimney inspections
Yes — homeowner pulls the permit
No permit will be pulled for this job

question: Are fascia, soffit, and gutters on the new shed roof part of the contracted scope?
why_it_matters: Drawings show them but neither the proposal nor the breakdown carries them.
unblocks: Exterior trim/gutter tasks after roofing, trim material procurement

choices: Fascia and soffit yes, no gutters
Fascia, soffit, and gutters all included
Fascia only
None — excluded from this job

question: Which customer selections are still outstanding: veneer, hearth, mantel, shingle match, screen door?
why_it_matters: Canon bars scheduling before final selections; outstanding items set procurement tasks and lead times.
unblocks: Selection/procurement tasks and their placement ahead of demo and finish phases

choices: Veneer (stone/tile)
Hearth material
Mantel
Shingle color/style match
Screen door
None — all selections final

question: Does the existing HVAC condenser sit inside or against the new patio footprint such that it must be moved?
why_it_matters: A relocation adds a mechanical trade ahead of demolition; protect-only adds nothing.
unblocks: Utility relocation task before demo, HVAC sub coordination, site protection

choices: Outside the footprint — protect only, no work
Against the knee wall — clearance issue, shift the pad a few feet
Inside the footprint — full relocation by HVAC sub before demo

question: Can a concrete truck and mini-excavator reach the rear-yard patio directly, or is a pump/buggy required?
why_it_matters: Access determines excavation method, pour method, and equipment for the concrete phase.
unblocks: Excavation and pour task durations, equipment rental, staging/protection tasks

choices: Direct truck and machine access via the side yard
Concrete pump truck needed; mini-excavator can reach
Wheelbarrow/buggy only for concrete and hand-dig excavation

question: How many sides of the porch are open and screened: two (inside corner per the plan) or three (per the breakdown's 60 LF)?
why_it_matters: Screen wall footage drives knee-wall/vinyl, screen framing, and post counts by roughly 40%.
unblocks: checklist item siding (Siding (WRB, siding, tie-in blend))

choices: Two sides (~36 LF, house on two sides)
Three sides (~60 LF)

question: Is the beam carrying the rafters over the open screen side dimensional lumber or an LVL?
why_it_matters: An LVL beam is a separate engineered-member order with a longer lead than the framing package.

choices: Built-up dimensional lumber (double 2x10/2x12)
LVL beam
6x6/6x8 solid PT timber
Undecided until sizing is done

question: Is there a finished ceiling (beadboard or T&G) under the shed rafters, or do the rafters stay exposed?
why_it_matters: A ceiling finish is a separate multi-day carpentry and material package that appears in the drawings but not the proposal.

choices: Exposed rafters, no ceiling finish
Beadboard ceiling
Tongue-and-groove pine ceiling
Painted plywood/soffit-panel ceiling

question: Do any existing vents (dryer, range hood, plumbing stack, bath fan) on the rear wall or roof land under the new shed roof?
why_it_matters: Vents terminating under a screened roof must be rerouted or extended, adding a task before roofing closes in.
unblocks: checklist item appliance_vent_extension (Extend existing appliance vents through new roof)

choices: No existing vents in the tie-in area
One plumbing stack on the existing roof must be extended
Dryer or exhaust vent on the rear wall must be rerouted
Unknown until walls are checked on site
